choices.pr_choice: The two distributivity theorems are named `commutator_sup_left` (join in the first commutator argument) and `commutator_sup_right` (join in the second).
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_right (N H K : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅N, H ⊔ K⁆ = ⁅N, H⁆ ⊔ ⁅N, K⁆ := by
choices.consequence: The names are how users find the lemmas. Here `_left`/`_right` say which commutator argument holds the join, which could also be read as left/right distributivity; another name changes discoverability and later naming of siblings.

choices.pr_choice: Stated as one equality of subgroups with the commutator of the join on the left and the join of the two commutators on the right.
choices.consequence: The orientation decides what `rw`/`simp only` with the lemma does (distribute vs collect); stating inequalities separately or the reverse orientation would change how callers use it.

choices.pr_choice: All three subgroups are explicit arguments of their own (not the file's section variables), normality is an instance-implicit `[N.Normal]`, and the argument order is H K N for the left form and N H K for the right form.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_left (H K N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆ := by
choices.consequence: Explicit versus implicit subgroups and the argument order change every term-mode use and rewrite; an instance-implicit normality hypothesis must be found by instance search rather than passed as a local proof.

choices.pr_choice: The hypothesis is that N is normal in the whole group G, not a weaker condition such as N normalized by H and K.
choices.excerpt: prove `⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆ = ⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆` for `N` normal
choices.status_reason: The title and the description's first paragraph both state the result for N normal; capability 2.1.
choices.visibility_reason: The result cannot be stated without its hypothesis; whether a weaker one is wanted is left as an open question.
choices.consequence: A weaker hypothesis (N normalized by H and K) would cover subgroups that are normal only in a smaller group; normality in G forces callers to supply a global Normal instance.

choices.pr_choice: Only binary joins H ⊔ K are covered; there is no version for an indexed join of a family of subgroups.
choices.consequence: An indexed version would serve users with families of subgroups and would imply the binary one; binary-only is the minimal surface.

choices.pr_choice: The mirrored form, with the join in the second commutator argument, is provided as a separate public theorem.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_sup_right (N H K : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] : ⁅N, H ⊔ K⁆ = ⁅N, H⁆ ⊔ ⁅N, K⁆ := by
choices.consequence: Without it, users with the join in the second argument must first rewrite with commutator symmetry; with it, there are two lemmas to keep in sync.

choices.pr_choice: The two distributivity theorems carry no attributes: no `to_additive` (so no additive-subgroup analogue) and no `simp`, while the helper lemmas added alongside them are `to_additive`.
choices.consequence: Users of commutators of additive subgroups get the helpers but not the main result; a later contributor must add the additive analogue; simp-tagging would change what simp does with commutators of joins.

choices.pr_choice: The proof restricts to the join M = H ⊔ K ⊔ N via `subgroupOf`, shows that M normalizes [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] using normalizer lemmas, and computes in the quotient by that subgroup via the centralizer criterion.
choices.excerpt: The idea is to compute `⁅H ⊔ K, N⁆` in the quotient `(H ⊔ K ⊔ N) ⧸ (⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆)`.
choices.consequence: A different route, for example an elementwise commutator identity, might need neither the private auxiliary lemma nor the helper lemmas nor access to the normalizer lemma from the commutator file, so the route bears on how much of the API change is needed; the length of the proof also bears on maintenance.

choices.pr_choice: An auxiliary version assuming only that [H, N] ⊔ [K, N] is normal is added as a `private` theorem with a primed name.
choices.excerpt: private theorem commutator_sup_left' (H K N : Subgroup G) [(⁅H, N⁆ ⊔ ⁅K, N⁆).Normal] :
choices.consequence: It is a variant under a different hypothesis; keeping it private keeps it out of the API, while making it public would offer that variant to users and commit to maintaining it.

choices.pr_choice: The mirrored form is derived from the left form by commutator symmetry.
Two new public lemmas give monotonicity of the commutator subgroup in one argument at a time, as special cases of the existing `commutator_mono`.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_mono_left (h : H₁ ≤ H₂) : ⁅H₁, K⁆ ≤ ⁅H₂, K⁆ :=
choices.consequence: Adds public API that restates special cases of `commutator_mono`; the names claim the one-sided monotonicity slot for later contributors.

choices.pr_choice: The one-sided monotonicity lemmas are registered with `gcongr` and `to_additive`.
choices.consequence: Registering them changes what `gcongr`/`grw` can do with commutator subgroups downstream; not registering them would leave such goals to manual monotonicity.

choices.pr_choice: A new public `to_additive` lemma says that [K₁, K₂] ≤ K when K₁ ≤ K and K₂ ≤ K.
choices.excerpt: theorem commutator_le_of_le (h₁ : K₁ ≤ K) (h₂ : K₂ ≤ K) : ⁅K₁, K₂⁆ ≤ K :=
choices.consequence: New public API with a generic `_of_le` name that is a one-line consequence of `commutator_le_sup`; it adds surface to maintain and claims a name.

choices.pr_choice: The one-sided monotonicity lemmas go right after `commutator_mono`, the upper-bound lemma right after `commutator_le_sup`, and the distributivity theorems after `variable (H₁ H₂)` and before `commutator_characteristic`.
The new commutator results go in the existing commutator file.
The reorganization of the existing normalizer-of-a-join lemma is bundled into the same contribution as the new commutator result.

choices.consequence: Bundling an API rename into a feature PR enlarges the review; a separate PR would isolate the deprecation and the import change.

feasibility_reason: The main result can be stated in mathematical terms at the generality the title and description require (N normal), with the equation written neutrally, while the names, binders, argument order, orientation, attributes, helper lemmas, mirrored form, proof route and placement within files stay hidden. The reorganization of the existing normalizer lemma has to be reported, because it is one of the change's kinds and the description makes it part of the contribution. The brief names only the lemma's current name, says that its location and name are in scope, and says that references to the current name must keep working. Its new name, its position, the deprecation mechanism and date, and the new import stay hidden. The only consequential choice exposed beyond the stated goal is the target file Subgroup/Basic.lean, which the packet's base files reveal anyway.
brief_omits: The description's reason for the rename, aligning the name with the existing sibling `inf_normalizer_le_normalizer_inf`, is left out because it would effectively give the new name. The description's proof idea (second paragraph) is left out as a proof route. The new import of the commutator file into Pointwise.lean is a consequence of the design rather than a goal, so it is not listed as a maintenance kind. The helper lemmas (one-sided monotonicity, the upper bound, the private auxiliary variant) are left out. The equation's orientation, which the title shows, is stated neutrally as equality of the two subgroups.
